messages:
sophie: thinking aloud — should we surface SLO alert rules in the console down to per-route level or keep it service-wide? tradeoff: signal vs config noise
kevin: +1 to exposing them, but we need sane defaults. per-route makes sense for high-cardinality surfaces where latency/error patterns differ. otherwise teams will be overwhelmed
maya: agree. can we auto-suggest thresholds? e.g. show 95th latency baseline and propose 2x or +50ms from baseline as a threshold?
dmitri: auto-suggest is good. also need to show burn-rate style alerts (error_budget burn rate > 4x in 10m) vs instant threshold (p50>200ms). both are useful for different failure modes
sophie: what's the minimal notification model? many folks want pager for infra, but product teams prefer slack/email first
kevin: propose mapping: SEV=pager for burn-rate on critical service SLOs, slack for route-level degradations with aggregated counts, email for low-priority. Also dedupe notifications across routes (group by service) to avoid pager spam
lina: UI idea — per-SLO notification policy with a simple escalation matrix. A compact view: "SLO -> severity -> channels -> cooldown (mins)". Users can pick templates: "prod-critical", "prod-degraded", "dev"
ops-oncall: please add a global rate limit. last incident we got 400 pings in 10m because of a noisy cache-miss route. even grouped alerts spamed pager. a cap like 3 pages per 30m per team would help
dmitri: agree. implement server-side dedupe window + per-channel rate limit. Also allow silence/snooze at rule-level and service-level from console
sophie: UX question — if a rollout is tied to a SLO, should the console show a direct "pause rollout" action when burn-rate triggers?
kevin: yes — automatic canary rollback or pause is powerful but scary. show an explicit button and require a policy with opt-in. UI should show which rollouts will be affected and the error budget impact before action
maya: small sample policy snippet for discussion:
```yaml
slo:
  name: "chat-service-latency"
  window: 1h
  objective: 99.5
  alert:
    - type: "burn_rate"
      threshold: 4.0
      severity: "pager"
      cooldown_minutes: 30
    - type: "latency_percentile"
      percentile: 95
      threshold_ms: 500
      severity: "slack"
      cooldown_minutes: 15
notification:
  group_by: ["service"]
  dedupe_window_seconds: 300
  max_pages_per_team_per_30m: 3
```
kevin: +1. bring back a compact preview in the rule editor showing expected noise (based on last 7d traffic) and estimated alert count per day
sophie: sounds good. one more: we need runtime telemetry to show which model/route combo caused the alert (model version, quantization). that's critical for debugging and for rollout gating
dmitri: telemetry is in. we'll add fields to SLO events: `route`, `model_version`, `instance_type`, `seq_len_bucket`. should help filter in console
ops-bot: Deploy completed: rollout/42 -> chat-service @dmitri at 1768801500
ops-oncall: can we also expose a "quiet hours" policy per team so non-critical slack alerts are delayed overnight? reduces wakeups for global teams
lina: yep — part of notification templates. we'll prototype: timezone-aware quiet-hours, plus override for SEV>=pager
sophie: ok action items: 1) dmitri/kevin sketch server-side dedupe + rate limits 2) maya/lina mock console notification templates & compact noise preview 3) add rollout pause UX design 4) ops-oncall to write SLO incident runbook updates
kevin: I'll draft the dedupe design doc and include sample queries for expected alert volumes
dmitri: starting on event schema changes this week
maya: I'll mock screenshots by EOD Friday, will add the proposed suggested thresholds algorithm
sophie: thanks all — we'll review in next eng-platform sync. :thumbsup:
